intent: Polish Notifications and Settings drawers so they feel like cohesive FD-001/Oyatie Cloud command surfaces instead of prototype utility leftovers.
product_direction: Oyatie will build a hyperscaler-grade cloud substrate and dogfood all FD-001 microservices as tenant workloads on that substrate. FD-001 product delivery remains the master-plan product goal; Oyatie Cloud is the substrate that proves the platform can host real production tenants.
implementation_summary: Added dynamic and SSR-static utility backdrop so Notifications and Settings close like the command palette rather than floating as disconnected drawers.
Added Activity Center proof strip tying notifications to FD-001 close, filing, vendor, audit, Oyatie Cloud tenant workload previews, Work Hub, Evidence Spine, and Cloud Cells.
Added Settings proof strip tying preferences to FD-001, policy, identity, tenant catalog, and Oyatie Cloud posture with explicit no-mutation boundaries.
Added utility route actions and hydrated local feedback for Work Hub, evidence, cloud topology, identity, policy, and service catalog routes.
Styled proof strips and route buttons with existing dense command-surface tokens and responsive behavior.

visual_verdict.category_match: Cohesive FD-001/Oyatie Cloud utility command drawers
visual_verdict.reasoning: Notifications and Settings now read as utility command drawers in the same FD-001/Oyatie Cloud product system, with proof strips, route actions, local-only boundaries, and backdrop close parity.
differences: Utility drawers remain local visual controls; no backend persistence or provider mutation is wired by design.
suggestions: A future wiring pass can bind the drawer route actions to real tenant notification and preference APIs without altering the visual hierarchy.

commands.summary: ready-after-2s; one transient empty reply immediately after restart

known_limits: Visual prototype only; utility actions do not persist settings, send mail, mutate auth/IAM, change billing, call integrations, deploy resources, or mutate cloud/provider state.
This slice improves utility/header drawers; it does not prove the full dashboard/mockup objective complete.
